summary.what_changed: Added three new project-memory rules to CLAUDE.md distilled from the CCE-170/171/172/173 incident cycle: (1) before removing or fixing something that persists data by accident, check what else reads it, since a file committed by mistake can still be a durable record something depends on; (2) a detection mechanism shipped in place of a withdrawn fix must state its exit criterion (threshold and date) in the same PR, so a measured zero doesn't linger as an indefinitely-carried detector; (3) a zero returned from a key that doesn't exist in a schema looks identical to a genuine zero, so any 'absence' finding should be reported alongside a positive control proving the recording channel actually works.
summary.why: Each rule captures a concrete process lesson from real incidents in the CCE-170 through CCE-174 cycle: CCE-174 found that removing accidental persistence (a committed diagnostic file) destroyed the only durable archive of CCE-141 firing data another initiative depended on; CCE-141 itself was withdrawn without an exit criterion and sat producing zero findings for three weeks before anyone could answer whether the detector was still needed; and a 2026-09-13 investigation nearly mistook a nonexistent schema field's default zero for a genuine zero finding until a positive-control value was located in the same data. These rules are recorded so future agents avoid repeating the same failure modes.
